verdict.rationale: Alerting is a fair axis for an agent evaluation and observability platform, but the evidence never mentions alert rules, thresholds on error rates, cost, or eval scores, or notification delivery. The closest items are a marketing claim of real-time production agent monitoring, which is adjacent rather than alerting, and Slack appearing only as a simulated twin data source, not a notification channel. Scorer pass thresholds decide whether each check passed; they are not alerts.

support.subject: As a developer, I can set alerts on error rates, cost spikes, or eval-score drops and get notified in Slack, PagerDuty, or email
